open_issues: Two csproj edits go beyond the 'ProjectReferences only' rule and both were unavoidable. (1) src/Wakeel.Admin.UI: added PackageReference to QRCoder and ZXing.Net (drawing the recovery QR and reading one back from a picture, both required by the spec) plus <EmbeddedResource Include="Migrations\*.sql" /> for the admin migration set. Both packages are already pinned in Directory.Packages.props (Wakeel.UI uses them) — no new package was introduced and Directory.Packages.props was not touched. (2) src/Wakeel.Admin: SDK changed from Microsoft.NET.Sdk to Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor, exactly as Wakeel.Desktop, because the plain SDK produces no static-web-asset manifest and the host then serves neither _content/Wakeel.Design/css/* nor the scoped-CSS bundle — the window compiled but rendered unstyled.

The design image for A01 shows a grid of twelve 8-character one-time codes; the B1 specification and this task both call for a single 20-character recovery code plus its QR (and Wakeel.Crypto's RecoveryCode implements exactly that). I built the spec version and the sheet shows one grouped code XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXC with its QR beside it. If the owner wants the twelve-code sheet instead, that is a crypto-side change (twelve independent wraps) and belongs in a decision, not in this package.

A02's design shows a «تذكر هذا الجهاز 8 ساعات» tick box. Deliberately not built: it would mean a DPAPI machine wrap of the admin.db key, and a machine wrap means whoever carries the computer away opens the organisation's signing keys. AdminDpapiProtector is registered (admin-2/3 need a protector for setup files and maintenance) but admin.db itself opens only with the password or the printed sheet. Worth an owner decision before anyone adds it.

The audit row for wrong passwords is written on the next successful sign-in, as a count, not at the moment of the failure — the database cannot be opened while the password is still wrong, so there is nowhere to write it. The counter and the lock-out themselves live in keys/admin.key (no secrets in it) so a restart cannot clear them; there is a test for that.

CoreWebView2 in the pinned Microsoft.Web.WebView2 1.0.4191.47 has ShowPrintUI (void), not ShowPrintUIAsync, so «طباعة الورقة» opens the system print dialogue and returns at once; the screen therefore reports only that the dialogue opened and never claims something came out of the printer. «حفظ نسخة PDF» uses PrintToPdfAsync and does report truthfully. Note that src/Wakeel.Desktop/Services/WebView2PrintService.cs still calls ShowPrintUIAsync and will not compile against this package version — that file is outside my paths, so I left it alone; its owner should know.

Tabs A04–A11 are drawn in the strip but go nowhere until admin-2/admin-3 add their pages. AdminRoutes already names every route and carries a `Built` set — each sub-package adds its own route to that set when it adds the page, and nothing else has to change. Same for A03's «تصدير ملف الإعداد» button.

Blazor's <InputFile> is used for picking the QR picture in A02's recovery dialog. It works in the host; the bUnit tests cover the 'this host cannot read pictures' path but not an actual decode, because decoding is the Windows imaging stack's job (AdminWindowsImagePixels) and that needs a WPF thread the test project does not have.
notes:
DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING

Storage. admin.db is opened with a random 32-byte key that exists only inside two wraps in keys/admin.key: one the password opens through Argon2id, one the 20-character recovery code opens the same way. Nothing derives the database key from the password, so changing the password re-wraps the same key instead of re-keying the file — which is why the printed sheet keeps working after a password change (tested). The attempt counter and the doubling lock-out live in admin.key, not in the database, because they must be read and written while the password is still wrong; a restart therefore cannot clear them (tested).

Schema. DATA-MODEL §13 is its own migration set, Migrations/0001_admin.sql, applied by AdminSchemaMigrator inside Wakeel.Admin.UI — deliberately a separate migrator from Wakeel.Core's SchemaMigrator, which is hard-bound to Wakeel.Core's embedded scripts, so neither set can ever be applied to the other's file. Bookkeeping table and rules are identical. No §0 columns, no change-log triggers, no EF model: the tool is the single writer and nothing here is synchronised. Every secret in a row (org private seeds, office key, device key seed) is AEAD-sealed with the database key before it is written.

Org keys. AdminKeyService.CreateOrganisation() generates the Ed25519/X25519 pair at A01, issues the self-signed root via DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot(orgId, identity, now), stores the certificate and the sealed seeds in the single `org` row, and never keeps the identity open between actions — OpenOrgIdentity() hands out a DeviceIdentity the caller disposes.

Audit. AdminAuditService is the writer only (A11's screen is admin-3's). It refuses a details object carrying any key whose name contains password/passphrase/secret/key/seed/recovery/code/wrap/token, rather than trusting each caller to remember; there is a test that walks every row written across a whole create/fail/sign-in/recover sequence and asserts neither password nor the printed code appears anywhere.

Composition. AddWakeelAdmin(paths) is the one root; AddAdminAccount() is admin-1's own slice. Every registration is TryAdd, and the three host-supplied seams (IAdminPrintService, IAdminImagePixels, IAdminWindow) have do-nothing defaults so a test host renders and says so in words instead of failing. admin-2 and admin-3 add AddAdminStructure()/AddAdminExport() beside the existing call and their own AdminAr.*.cs partials; no file of mine needs editing.

SCREEN-BY-SCREEN FIDELITY (launched from bin with --data-folder on a temp folder, CDP answered on 9334, drove the whole first run, screenshotted every screen light and dark, read the log, killed the process)

A01 — matches the design closely: thin bar with the tool's name and the machine line, two columns, numbered ① / ② badges on the cards, red «تُعرض هذه الورقة مرة واحدة فقط» panel, the sheet with the organisation name, issue date, administrator, the code in a monospace LTR-isolated box beside its QR, the three actions (طباعة / حفظ PDF / نسخ الرمز), the «طبعتُ الورقة وحفظتها» tick box, and a command strip with «الخروج» left and the primary button right. «ابدأ» renders disabled until the box is ticked (verified live and in bUnit). Divergences: the single 20-character code replaces the design's twelve-code grid (see open_issues); the rule ticks use the design system's `minus`/`check-circle` icons since no circle-outline icon exists in the registry; after creation step one shows a green «أُنشئ حساب مدير النظام» panel rather than the disabled filled fields the mock implies — the password has left the screen by then and a meter still reading «قصيرة جدًا» would have been a lie.

A02 — matches: centred card on an empty frame, mark, tool name, organisation name under it (the key file carries the name precisely so this line can exist before the database opens), title, description, password field, the standing «يُقفل الدخول 30 ثانية بعد 5 محاولات خاطئة» note, full-width «دخول», the recovery link, and the machine line at the foot. The lock-out replaces the note with a red panel and a live countdown that ticks once a second. The recovery path swaps the card in place: code field, «اختيار صورة الرمز», new password and its confirmation, and a note that the sheet stays valid. Divergence: no «تذكر هذا الجهاز 8 ساعات» (see open_issues).

A03 — matches: dark bar with the mark, «مدير نظام الوكيل», the organisation summary line, theme and sign-out icon buttons (both with tooltips), the administrator's name and role and avatar; the seven-tab strip exactly as DESIGN-GUIDE lists them; page header with title, sub-line and «تحديث» + «تصدير ملف الإعداد» on the far side; four KPI cards (الهيكلية 0/0/0, المكاتب المفعّلة, الأجهزة المسجّلة, آخر تصدير); and the two panels, «الهيكلية بإيجاز» and «تنبيهات», each with its own empty state written as an invitation rather than an error. Every figure is read live from the tables — the seeded test fills the org_units/offices/devices/setup_exports/pending_changes rows admin-2 and admin-3 will write, and the board counts them, lists one line per department and raises all three alert kinds without any change to this code.

RTL/bidi (item 55): dir="rtl" on the root, <Bdi> around every organisation name, administrator name, machine name and composed count line, Bidi.Wrap on mixed sentences built in C#, `direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate` on the recovery code box, logical CSS properties throughout (padding-inline, border-block-end, margin-inline). Every icon-only button (home, theme, sign-out) carries both a tooltip and an aria-label. No screen shows a code, a number, a port, a server or a database name.
